speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mucous membranes, and petechiae. To understand the cause of this bleeding, have you noticed any bruising that appeared without injury or a family history of similar bleeding problems?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP).

The clinical presentation of petechiae, mucous membrane bleeding, and unexplained bruising in a 4-year-old male is classic for ITP. To confirm this, please return the results for a Complete Blood Count (CBC) and a Peripheral Blood Smear.
